items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: I'll tell you the band that had the real readers in it, P-Rong, A.J. P-Rong.

ctx.x: Yeah, I remember that piece. Well now who were the bands that played mostly society music, just reading, no Dixieland?

Well Tuxedo, very little reading they had though, I ain't going to lie. I'll tell you the band that had the real readers in it, P-Rong, A.J. P-Rong. Did they play any Dixieland? They played Dixieland but they played a lot of the music, beautiful numbers and things you know? Yeah. Yeah.
And what about Celestan's Tuxedo? What would he feature?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: He was a straight reader, but he played out there with P. Ron.

ctx.x: He was a straight reader, but he played out there with P. Ron. And Kemba was a straight reader, but he could... He could...

But all them boys was out there in the field like me, all them got off, I ain't kidding, every one of them. Every one of them. Now this Louis Demand, he didn't get off, but he always had good music. What about a guy like Kaza? Kaza played with Sackton. Clarinet and Sackton. Clarinet and Sackton, yeah, he played good, but I never did wake with Kaza. Was he a get off man? Yeah, he played pretty good. He used to play with that tall face of Teach. Teach right here, you know him. What a guy's name in there. He was the…

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: Not Fate Marble, I mean, P. Ron. A.J. P. Ron.

ctx.x: Uh, uh, uh, Fate Marble. Not Fate Marble, I mean, P. Ron. A.J. P. Ron.
You worked with P. Ron, huh? Sure.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: We were really nice together, but I never did play with him.

ctx.x: do that anymore. They got your book. That's what we're doing, we're working on that book, you know, the guy that put the book out, it's a friend of mine, he lives in Slidell. We're working on all that. Let me see now, did you ever work with B-Rod? No. Never did, huh?
No. We were really nice together, but I never did play with him. Did Sid Ann any with him?
No. I just thought maybe you knew some of the different guys that worked with him. No,
